title: OFA architecture code plus Mirror function code
hypothesis: On one shared width/depth/kernel-elastic supernetwork, a compact configuration-conditioned Givens correction will improve unseen configuration quality over native subnet selection and beat a byte-matched generic rank-one output correction without storing independent subnet weights.
physical_object: One fixed 12-channel residual supernetwork with shared input, recurrent hidden, and output maps
mirror_coordinate: Three FP32 coefficients mapping normalized width, depth and kernel configuration to one Givens angle applied to active hidden channels
logical_multiplicity: Eight width/depth/kernel subnet functions, including four held-out joint configurations
controls: native elastic subnet with no correction
configuration-conditioned rank-one output correction with comparable bytes
independent full output map per configuration upper reference

development.selection_metric: held-out configuration normalized MSE; no hyperparameter tuning on heldout

paid_objects: rank-one correction factors and configuration coefficients

success_gate: On all three fresh worlds, Mirror heldout NRMSE <=1e-4, improves native subnet NRMSE by >=10%, uses <=50% bytes of independent maps, and uses >=10% fewer bytes than the byte-matched generic correction at comparable quality.
failure_gate: Any fresh world misses quality or byte gates, or generic direct correction matches Mirror quality within 10% at equal/lower bytes.
boundaries: Synthetic OFA-like mechanism test only; no OFA checkpoint, progressive shrinking training, ImageNet, hardware-specific latency, or GPU evidence.
Teacher uses a smooth width/depth/kernel Givens orbit, intentionally favorable to the mechanism.
No optimizer updates; test is calibration/interpolation, not capacity or trained supernet evidence.
